title: Reading
description: A small shelf of humane stories, with a commonplace book of Song ci fragments.
heading: A few pages worth keeping.

sections.heading: Ordinary lives, closely read.
sections.intro: A starting shelf of stories about companionship, loss, and the possibility of beginning again. These short introductions leave room for personal notes to come.

books.title: The Unlikely Pilgrimage of Harold Fry
books.author: Rachel Joyce
books.blurb: A retired man goes out to post a letter and keeps walking. The journey gives old regrets a physical shape: distance, tired feet, unexpected company. A good place to begin for readers drawn to an unhurried story about what people carry, and what they might still put down.
books.sourceLabel: About the book · Penguin Random House

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.originalTitle: 《一个叫欧维的男人决定去死》
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.blurb: Ove has rules for almost everything, and little patience for the neighbours who keep breaking them. Beneath the friction sits a story about grief and the practical ways people look after one another. For readers who enjoy humour with tenderness just below the surface.

books.title: My Grandmother Asked Me to Tell You She’s Sorry
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.blurb: A grandmother’s letters send seven-year-old Elsa into the complicated lives of her neighbours. Fairy tales and ordinary rooms gradually begin to overlap. For readers interested in how stories can make unfamiliar people more understandable, without making them less strange.

books.title: The Storied Life of A.J. Fikry
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.blurb: A bookseller’s shrinking world opens unexpectedly around a small island bookshop. Books here become a way to find company and pass something on. A natural next read for anyone who likes stories in which a place, and the people who gather there, matter as much as the plot.

excerpts.text:
莫聽穿林打葉聲，
何妨吟嘯且徐行。
excerpts.translation:
Let the rain strike leaves beyond the path.
Why not hum a little, and walk on slowly?
excerpts.author: Su Shi · 蘇軾

excerpts.text:
無可奈何花落去，
似曾相識燕歸來。
excerpts.translation:
Beyond our keeping, the blossoms fall;
swallows return with the look of an old acquaintance.
excerpts.author: Yan Shu · 晏殊

excerpts.text:
知否，知否，
應是綠肥紅瘦。
excerpts.translation:
Have you noticed, have you noticed?
The leaves must be fuller now; the blossoms fewer.
excerpts.author: Li Qingzhao · 李清照
excerpts.sourceUrl: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/如夢令_(李清照)/如夢令_(昨夜雨疏風驟)
